entities.summary: Thibron was a Spartan general who played a significant role in the Ionian Revolt against the Persian Empire in the 390s BCE. He was sent out as harmost in 400 BC, with an army of about 5,000 men, composed of 1,000 Neodamodes and 4,000 other Peleponesians, to aid the Ionians against Tissaphernes, who wished to bring them into subjection. In addition to this force, Thibron recruited 2,000 local troops upon his arrival, but was initially unable to face the Persian army in the field. However, after he was joined by elements of the Ten Thousand, he was able to seize several cities. He then, after a series of brilliant military maneuvers, was able to defeat the Persians and secure a significant victory for the Ionians. This victory had far-reaching consequences, as it marked a significant turning point in the Ionian Revolt and paved the way for the eventual independence of the Ionian cities from Persian rule. Thibron's military tactics and strategic decisions during this campaign have been studied by historians for centuries, and he remains one of the most celebrated figures of the ancient Greek world. Despite his many achievements, however, Thibron's life and legacy are not well documented, and much of what we know about him comes from the accounts of ancient historians such as Xenophon. Nevertheless, his impact on the course of history is undeniable, and he remains an important figure in the annals of ancient Greek history.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Thibron's victory marked a significant turning point in the Ionian Revolt, and paved the way for the eventual independence of the Ionian cities from Persian rule. He remains one of the most celebrated figures of the ancient Greek world, and his military tactics and strategic decisions during this campaign have been studied by historians for centuries.
